## TRA Timeline

#### Up-C reorganization and TRA execution

- 2015-06-05: Up-C reorganization closes; Reit Management & Research Trust (Portnoy family vehicle) contributes its interest in REIT Management & Research LLC in exchange for Class A Units and Class B shares; TRA executed between RMR Inc., the LLC, and RMR Trust, paying 85% of cash tax savings from basis step-ups on initial Class A Unit purchase and future redemptions, plus imputed interest deductions
- 2015-10-13: S-1 files the executed TRA as exhibit 10.17
- 2015-12-14: IPO consummated

#### Trust rename and Tax Act remeasurement

- 2016-01-20: Reit Management & Research Trust converts from Massachusetts business trust to Maryland statutory trust and renames to ABP Trust; same legal entity, no TRA amendment
- 2018-fiscal-year: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act enacted December 22, 2017; phased corporate-rate reduction prompts $24.7M reduction in TRA liability on the FY18 income statement as "Tax Receivable Agreement remeasurement". In-force remeasurement, not an amendment

## Explanation

The RMR Group's Up-C reorganization on June 5, 2015 (preceding the December 2015 IPO) created a TRA paying 85% of cash tax savings to RMR Trust (later renamed ABP Trust, the Portnoy family vehicle), covering basis step-ups from the initial Class A Unit purchase and future redemptions plus imputed interest deductions on TRA payments themselves. The trust counterparty was renamed and converted from a Massachusetts business trust to a Maryland statutory trust on January 20, 2016 without amending the TRA, and the FY18 enactment of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act prompted a $24.7M remeasurement of the liability for the lower corporate rate. No amendments and no terminations have been filed across ten fiscal years of 10-Ks; the contract remains in force and pays out routinely. The September 30, 2025 TRA liability was $15.9M (down from $18.4M at year-end FY24). See `contract_log.md` for the full filing-by-filing record and the inventory of TRA-adjacent filings that do not amend the contract.
